newsitem.title: USA: ASARCO forecasts continued silver deficit.
newsitem.headline: ASARCO forecasts continued silver deficit.

text.p: The silver market deficit is set to continue over the next two years as consumption outstrips supply, Richard de J Osborne, chairman, president and chief executive of ASARCO, said.
"In 1997 and 1998 we expect consumption to continue to grow at a rate greater than the growth in supply," Osborne told an analysts briefing.
This will take the supply deficit from 133 million ounces last year, to 144 million ounces this year, and 149 million ounces in 1998.
COMEX silver stocks should continue to decline in the light of the continued supply deficit, Osborne said.
"We have been expecting a sustained improvement in prices for some time," Osborne said, adding that recent gains may well be a harbinger of this.
COMEX silver prices rallied nearly 10 percent this week due to fund buying. COMEX silver stocks now stand at 194 million ounces.
ASARCO refined 32 million ounces of silver last year.
